note: Seeded from the owner session on 2026-08-23 against the full fact sheet (watch curves, view sources, per-channel subscribers and watch shares, health reads, live, platform split). recommendations.mjs regenerates this store when the pipeline runs with an API key.

items.text: Every episode loses its crowd at the door: around 70.4% of starters are watching near the open, and only 11.7–14.9% remain by the 2% mark — the largest single loss anywhere in the show.
items.recommendation: Rebuild the first 90 seconds: cold-open the strongest exchange, move intros and housekeeping after it, and check the next episode's open against that 14.9% high-water mark.

items.text: Goodbye, Blank Canvas is the watch-time winner at 13.2% of the video seen on average; every other episode sits between 8.9 and 12.9%.
items.recommendation: Break down what its first 5 minutes do differently and reuse that structure for the next two openings; compare their finished health reads against 33 and 44.

items.text: End screens have produced 7 views across the entire catalog — a free surface at the exact moment the remaining audience is most committed.
items.recommendation: Add an end screen on both channels linking the next episode and the subscribe button; it costs nothing and every finished viewer sees it.

items.text: 54.7% of YouTube views come from subscriptions and home while search brings 5% — current packaging mostly reaches people the show already has.
items.recommendation: Package the next launch for strangers: title and thumbnail on the guest's topic as someone would search it, then watch whether search and suggested move.

items.text: X carries 56.7% of all watching (12,710 of 22,436 views), but a viewer can only subscribe on YouTube — the biggest audience never gets asked.
items.recommendation: Pin the YouTube link as the first reply under both hosts' announce posts and say the YouTube handoff out loud as each live ends.

items.text: Subscriber pull spent itself on launch day one: 8.9 subscribers per 1,000 views on the first episode, then 2.9 or less on every episode since.
items.recommendation: Script one spoken subscribe ask at minute 2–3, right where the drop levels off, plus a pinned comment with the link — and judge it against that 8.9 start.

items.text: The two YouTube channels pull differently: Dive Club holds 11.1% of the video watched and adds 3.4 subscribers per 1,000 views; DesignerTom holds 9.7%, adds 2.2, and has added 0 subscribers since the July 23 episode.
items.recommendation: Lead launches on Dive Club and give DesignerTom a distinct cut — a shorter edit or a different angle — instead of the same upload twice; recheck both channels on the next episode.
